q: Electrolytic process is the use of electrolysis by which _____ substances are decomposed when an electric current is passed through them.
e: Electrolytic process is the use of electrolysis by which ionic substances are decomposed when an electric current is passed through them. Electrolysis uses electrical energy to force a non-spontaneous chemical change. Ionic is the word this version is asking about.

q: In the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, $Na^+$ ions accept electrons and discharge at the _____.
e: In the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, Na^+ ions accept electrons and discharge at the cathode. Electrolysis uses electrical energy to force a non-spontaneous chemical change. The cathode is the electrode where reduction occurs.

q: In the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, $Cl^-$ ions give up electrons and discharge at the _____.
e: In the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, Cl^- ions give up electrons and discharge at the anode. Electrolysis uses electrical energy to force a non-spontaneous chemical change. The anode is the electrode where oxidation occurs.

q: The net result of electrolysis of molten sodium chloride is that liquid sodium floats to the top and _____ gas bubbles out of the melt above the anode.

q: The preferential discharge of ions depends on the position of metal ions or groups in the electrochemical series, the concentration of electrolyte and the _____ of the electrode used.

An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current. Electrodes are the conductors where oxidation and reduction happen during electrolysis. q: If all other factors are equal, any ion _____ in the electrochemical series will be discharged from the solution in preference to those above it.
